note: P-CABs reached GERD patients on rat/dog acid-secretion pharmacology; vonoprazan's dog-over-lansoprazole advantage carried into erosive oesophagitis healing, while the rodent ECL-carcinoid prediction has not appeared in 5-year human biopsies.
label: GERD (P-CABs)

engagement.model: Pylorus-ligated (Shay) rat and histamine-stimulated dog acid secretion
engagement.note: SCH 28080, the prototype P-CAB, cut acid output in pylorus-ligated rats and histamine-stimulated dogs; no patient comparison.
engagement.short: Prototype P-CAB blocks acid in rat and dog
engagement.quote: The antisecretory ED50 values in the pylorus-ligated rat were 3.7 mg/kg p.o. and 2.8 mg/kg i.p., being 7 and 10 times more potent than cimetidine, respectively.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level; J Pharmacol Exp Ther 226:114-120 carries no DOI in PubMed, so the PubMed URL is given. SCH 28080 never reached patients (hepatotoxic), so the model existed 27 years before vonoprazan's rat/dog work (Hori 2010, doi:10.1124/jpet.110.170274; Hori 2011, doi:10.1124/jpet.111.179556).

engagement.model: Rat and dog histamine-stimulated acid secretion (Hori 2011)
engagement.note: Single doses gave dose-dependent 24-h pH>=4 holding in healthy men; the authors say the animal prediction held.
engagement.short: Human pH holding matched animal prediction
engagement.quote: These results support those observed in preclinical animal studies and were predicted based on the compound's high accumulation.
engagement.reason: Human pH holding matched dog/rat prediction
engagement.judgement: Open-access full text read (PMC4816246); the Discussion sentence is the only explicit model-to-human comparison found for the class, and it is qualitative (direction only). Supporting juxtaposition: Hori 2011 found vonoprazan more potent and longer-lasting than lansoprazole in rats and dogs; Sakurai 2015 APT (doi:10.1111/apt.13325) found 24-h pH>=4 holding 24.6% higher than esomeprazole in healthy men, and Jenkins 2015 (doi:10.1111/apt.13121; NCT02123953/NCT02141711, no results posted) reported 93-100% pH>4 holding at 40 mg. Comparison is in healthy volunteers, not patients; Dent 2008 measured pH>4 time 75% vs 60% for AZD0865 75 mg vs esomeprazole 20 mg in NERD patients (doi:10.1111/j.1572-0241.2007.01544.x), same direction.

dose.model: Rat and dog acid-secretion dose-response (ED50, mg/kg)
dose.note: Dog ED50 for the prototype P-CAB; vonoprazan's rat 4 mg/kg and dog 1 mg/kg were never compared with its 20 mg human dose.
dose.short: Animal mg/kg never compared with human dose
dose.quote: In dogs, SCH 28080 was effective in inhibiting acid secretion stimulated by histamine (ED50 of 0.09 mg/kg i.v. and 4.4 mg/kg p.o.), dimaprit, pentagastrin, insulin and feeding.
dose.judgement: Vonoprazan fully blocked rat acid secretion at 4 mg/kg (Hori 2010, doi:10.1124/jpet.110.170274) and tegoprazan blocked dog secretion at 1.0 mg/kg (Takahashi 2018, doi:10.1124/jpet.117.244202); human doses (vonoprazan 20 mg ~0.3 mg/kg; label Table 11: 85.2% of 24 h at pH>4 on day 7) were set by clinical dose-ranging. Jenkins 2015 Methods use the dog NOAEL AUC only as an exposure ceiling. AZD0865 25/50/75 mg healed EE equally (Kahrilas 2007), i.e. no human dose-response, but no animal dose prediction for AZD0865 was ever published (dog data appear only in the Andersson & Carlsson 2005 review, doi:10.1016/j.pharmthera.2005.05.005), so nothing to score.

efficacy.model: Rat acid-injury (ulcer) models and dog 24-h acid secretion
efficacy.note: Prototype P-CAB healed rat ulcer models; the class's GERD claim rests on 24-h acid control in dogs, with no patient comparison.
efficacy.quote: SCH 28080 (1-30 mg/kg p.o.) also inhibited gastric ulcers provoked by aspirin, aspirin + acid, indomethacin and stress (cold-restraint) in rats.
efficacy.judgement: No reflux-oesophagitis animal model was used for the class until tegoprazan (Kim 2019 rat GERD model, doi:10.1124/jpet.118.254904); vonoprazan's efficacy case was the dog/rat acid-control advantage over lansoprazole (Hori 2011).

efficacy.model: Rat and dog histamine-stimulated acid secretion vs lansoprazole (Hori 2011)
efficacy.note: Vonoprazan healed more EE than lansoprazole, the PPI it beat in rats and dogs; AZD0865 had only matched esomeprazole.
efficacy.short: Vonoprazan beats lansoprazole in EE healing
efficacy.quote: Among 1024 patients in the healing phase, vonoprazan was noninferior to lansoprazole in the primary analysis and superior on the exploratory analysis of healing (92.9 vs 84.6%; difference, 8.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.5%-12.2%).
efficacy.judgement: Juxtaposed by me: Laine (PHALCON-EE, NCT04124926, results posted 2022-07-29) does not cite the animal data; the label's Table 13 (93% vs 85%, difference 8%) agrees. Earlier non-inferiority trials (Ashida 2016 Japan; Xiao 2020 Asia, NCT02388724, results posted 2019-06-03) were not verified within budget and could move this year earlier. Not 'neg': no model flagged AZD0865 (linaprazan), which healed EE no better than esomeprazole 40 mg at 25/50/75 mg (Kahrilas 2007, doi:10.1016/j.cgh.2007.08.014; NCT00206245, no results posted) despite 75% vs 60% pH>4 time in NERD (Dent 2008). Its acid-control prediction held; the surrogate-to-healing link did not, and reviews attribute the commercial failure to a ~1 h half-life. No published model explained it, and AstraZeneca's AZD0865 dog data exist only inside the Andersson & Carlsson 2005 review.

safety.model: 2-year rat and mouse carcinogenicity (hypergastrinaemia to ECL-cell neuroendocrine tumours)
safety.note: VISION set up a 5-year biopsy trial to test the rodent hypergastrinaemia-ECL tumour prediction in patients.
safety.short: 5-year biopsy trial set to test rodent carcinoids
safety.quote: The primary endpoint of the study is the histopathological evaluation of gastric mucosa for the presence of neoplastic alteration of gastric mucosal epithelial cells.
safety.judgement: The rodent model is named in the Voquezna label 13.1 (24-month rat and mouse studies; rat neuroendocrine cell tumours at >=5 mg/kg/day; https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=0cc52ac5-77ec-4d66-a770-762a1a960914), so model_filed is true, but the year that carcinogenicity study was run is not published (it predates the 2015 Japanese approval), hence model_first_use_year null. VISION registry NCT02679508 first posted 2016-02-10.

safety.model: 2-year rat and mouse carcinogenicity (hypergastrinaemia to ECL-cell neuroendocrine tumours)
safety.note: Five years on, gastrin ran 3x higher than lansoprazole yet no neuroendocrine tumours; FDA calls the rodent finding rodent-specific.
safety.short: Rodent carcinoids not seen in 5-year biopsies
safety.quote: No malignant alterations or gastric neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) were observed; there was 1 adenoma in each group.
safety.reason: Rodent ECL tumours absent at 5 years
safety.judgement: Call: the model's tumour prediction did not hold (false positive), as with PPIs. The upstream mechanism did translate: median gastrin 625 vs 200 pg/mL and the label states 'Increased gastrin causes enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia and increased serum CgA levels' (12.2), while ECL hyperplasia was 4.9% vs 7.7% and 'No neoplastic changes were observed' in 135 biopsied patients; label 13.2 says 'This finding is considered to be a rodent-specific phenomenon.' Re-scoring to 'same' is defensible if the atlas counts the gastrin/ECL step as the prediction. 139 patients over 5 years cannot exclude rare NETs. comparison_stated false because Uemura does not set rodent data beside the human data (the label does; abstract-level reading of Uemura). The 3-year interim (Haruma 2023, doi:10.1186/s12876-023-02772-w) already showed no neoplasia. Separately, AZD0865 caused reversible transaminase rises (Kahrilas 2007), with no published animal prediction either way; vonoprazan showed no ALT signal (Jenkins 2015).
